content.text:
The campaign ran from Saturday 21 November to the end of Sunday 29 November, UK time. It stopped on schedule and is now expired, so nothing else will be charged. All four approved posts ran in both ad groups for the whole nine days, and X approved every one of them.

## Recap

| | Spend | Impressions | Link clicks | Cost per click |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Keywords: CI / DevOps** (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, CircleCI, Jenkins, flaky tests, CI/CD, DevOps, test automation) | $263.73 | 151,785 | 87 | $3.03 |
| **Interest: Software Development** | $227.54 | 115,299 | 63 | $3.61 |
| **Total** | **$491.27** | **267,084** | **150** | **$3.28** |

The total stayed under your $500 budget. Both ad groups were limited to the United Kingdom and Ireland, and were set to get as many link clicks as possible.

**What I changed:** after four days the keywords ad group was getting clicks more cheaply. On 25 November I moved $20 of the remaining budget from the interest group to the keywords group and raised the keywords group's daily cap from $28 to $34. Otherwise I checked delivery, spend and post approvals every day. Nothing came up that needed action.

**Which posts did best:** I last looked at results by post on 25 November, four days in. At that point the two offer-led posts got the most clicks per impression:
- "Until Sunday 29 November only…" (…542190) got 30 link clicks.
- "Nettle CI scores every test…" (…673400) got 21.

The "£0 for 60 days" post got 6 clicks and the "rerun job" post got 11. Both got plenty of impressions but few people went through to the site. I didn't pause them: four days of data on a small budget isn't enough to judge, and X's system was already showing the stronger posts more often.

**Comparing with your sign-ups:** without the pixel, X can't see sign-ups, so these numbers stop at the click. If you compare the 150 clicks with your sign-ups from 21–29 November, you'll get a rough cost per sign-up. Some sign-ups will have come from elsewhere, so treat it as a ceiling on what X delivered rather than an exact figure. If you plan to run X ads again, installing the pixel would let me judge results on sign-ups rather than clicks.
